target.title: feat: add editable voice dictation to the Control UI
target.body:
Closes #98026

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's Control UI offers realtime Talk, but users cannot dictate an ordinary editable chat draft. They must rely on inconsistent OS-level dictation or start a conversational realtime session that can invoke an agent instead of simply returning text.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a composer-native, independently written batch-dictation workflow: click the microphone or hold `Ctrl+M`, record with waveform/timer feedback, cancel or confirm, then review the transcript inserted at the captured selection before sending. The browser uses standard media APIs and the Gateway delegates to the existing `tools.media.audio` provider/CLI pipeline, so there is no second credential, model, or fallback stack.

The additive `audio.transcribe` method requires `operator.write`, accepts supported base64 audio up to 12 MB, writes only a private temporary file for path-based local transcribers, and removes it after every attempt. Browser recordings remain memory-only and stop after two minutes.

Alternatives rejected in the included ADR: browser Web Speech (inconsistent vendor/provider control), a dictation-only STT stack (duplicated policy), and realtime Talk (different product semantics).

## User Impact

Control UI users can dictate prompts, see live recording feedback, cancel safely, recover from permission/device/provider errors, and edit the transcript before sending. The workflow works with existing cloud STT providers or local Whisper CLI configuration. Setup, privacy controls, observable Cursor UX research, supported-browser notes, and the ADR are documented in `docs/web/dictation.md`.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/ui/chat/dictation-recorder.test.ts` — 5 passed

target.title: fix(tts): defer text settlement for final-mode TTS to eliminate churn (#83511)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.tts.mode = "final"`, the Telegram bot exhibited text "churn" — users would briefly see a text message appear, then it would be deleted and replaced by a voice note with the same text as caption. This happened on **both** the ACP dispatch path and the non-ACP dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.ts`).

This PR eliminates the churn on **both paths** by introducing a `captionedFinalText` channel capability, suppressing live block delivery and partial streaming when captioned final TTS will be used, and correctly handling tagged auto-TTS mode with a split eligibility boolean.

## Root cause

```
Before (main):
  1. Block text / partial streaming delivers text to user immediately
  2. TTS synthesis runs (2-5 seconds)
  3. Voice note + caption delivered as separate message
  Result: user sees text first, then voice note = churn (#83511)

After (this PR):
  1. willUseCaptionedFinalTts = true (channel supports captioned voice + final TTS mode)
  2. Partial streaming suppressed, block text delivery suppressed
  3. TTS synthesis runs, text accumulated silently
  4. Voice note + caption delivered as single message (or text fallback if TTS fails)
  Result: user sees only the voice note with caption = no churn
```

### Tagged auto-TTS mode

When `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"`, TTS only fires for replies containing `[[tts:...]]` directives. Three additional issues were discovered and fixed:

1. **Split boolean**: `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` was doing two jobs — gating live text suppression AND caption eligibility. Split into `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` (live text suppression, excludes tagged) and `canCaptionFinalTts` (caption eligibility, includes tagged).

2. **Block TTS gate**: The accumulated block TTS fallback was gated on `replies.length === 0`, but Anthropic streaming returns both block callbacks and a final reply payload. Changed to gate on `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` and `queuedFinal` instead.

3. **Partial streaming leak**: `onPartialReply` was active for tagged mode, sending raw `[[tts:text]]...[[/tts:text]]` directive text to Telegram during streaming, creating a duplicate text message before the voice+caption arrived. Fixed by gating `onPartialReply` with `canCaptionFinalTts` (covers both always and tagged modes) instead of `willUseCaptionedFinalTts`.

### Media block preservation

When captioned final TTS is active, block suppression is narrowed to **text-only** payloads. Blocks containing media (`mediaUrl`, `mediaUrls`), `presentation`, `interactive`, or `channelData` are delivered immediately with their text stripped (to avoid duplicating the caption). This applies to both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` + `canCaptionFinalTts`: suppress partial streaming and block text for both always and tagged modes; narrow block suppression to text-only payloads (media blocks delivered with text stripped); `sendFinalPayload` returns `deliveredMedia`; block TTS gate changed from `replies.length === 0` to `!deliveredFinalTtsMedia && !queuedFinal` |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | Regression tests: tagged directive-only voice+caption, tagged+always both-block-and-final delivery, partial suppression for tagged TTS on caption-capable channels, plain tagged block delivery, media block delivery with text stripped, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.ts` | `willUseCaptionedFinalTts` gate: suppress ACP block delivery and defer text settlement; `canCaptionFinalTts` for tagged mode; `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` tracking |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.ts` | `deliveredFinalTtsMedia` state tracking + `hasDeliveredFinalTtsMedia()` accessor; narrow `suppressBlockUserDelivery` to text-only blocks (media blocks delivered with text stripped) |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` | Regression tests: media block delivery with text stripped under `suppressBlockUserDelivery`, text-only block suppression |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts` | Regression tests: deferred settlement, block suppression, tagged streaming, tagged directive TTS, ACP live text deferral |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.ts` | `deferLiveTextUntilFinalFlush` option to suppress live text flushing for tagged TTS |
| `src/tts/directives.ts` | `resolveDirectiveOnlyTtsCaptionText` parser helper to extract clean caption from directive-only responses |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.ts` | `captionedFinalText: true` capability declaration |
| `extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts` | Test for capability declaration |
| `src/channels/plugins/types.core.ts` | JSDoc for `captionedFinalText` capability contract |
| `src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts` | Capability seam test |
| `docs/tools/tts.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability: opt-in criteria via `capabilities.tts.voice`, tagged mode behavior, text-only fallback, plugin API snippet |
| `docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins.md` | Document `captionedFinalText` capability in channel plugin SDK guide: opt-in declaration, media block preservation, fallback behavior, tagged mode |
| `docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256` | Updated SDK API baseline hash |

## Tests

```
$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
 ✓ 272 passed (272)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts
 ✓ 38 passed (38)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp.test.ts
 ✓ 67 passed (67)

$ npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.reply-dispatch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.final-outcome-counts.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.acp-abort.test.ts
 ✓ 26 passed (26)   # settle-lifecycle paths, no hang

$ npx vitest run extensions/telegram/src/shared.test.ts
 ✓ 11 passed (11)

$ npx vitest run src/channels/plugins/tts-capabilities.test.ts
 ✓ 1 passed (1)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Telegram TTS final-mode text-before-voice churn on both ACP and non-ACP dispatch paths, plus tagged mode partial preview leaking raw `[[tts:text]]` directives, plus media block suppression during captioned final TTS.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout at commit `05b4483a8f`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Live Telegram bot (`@thomas_fu_bot`) with Microsoft TTS (`zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural`), `messages.tts.mode: "final"`.

- **Failing proof before fix (live Telegram)**:

  ![Before fix — separate text message + voice message (churn)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-before-fix.png)

  User sent "hello" to the Telegram bot. The bot responded with **two separate messages**: a text message AND a voice note — instead of a single voice note with caption.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built and installed from current head: `npm run build && npm pack && npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz`
  2. Registered and restarted Gateway: `openclaw gateway install && openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Tested with `messages.tts.auto: "always"` and `messages.tts.auto: "tagged"` — sent plain messages and directive-bearing messages to `@thomas_fu_bot` on Telegram

- **Evidence after fix**: Always mode (`messages.tts.auto: "always"`) at commit `05b4483a8f`:

  ![Always mode — voice with caption, single message](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-always-mode.png)

  Always-mode replies produce a single voice note with caption text. No text churn, no separate text bubble.

- **Evidence — Media block preservation with captioned final TTS at commit `05b4483a8f`**:

  ![Media block preserved — image delivered + voice note with caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jerry-Xin/openclaw/proof-images-83988/.proof-images/83988-media-block.png)

  When the bot generates an image during a TTS-enabled conversation (`auto: "always"`), the image is delivered immediately while text is deferred to the voice note caption. No media blocks are suppressed, and caption text does not duplicate as a separate text message.

- **Observed result after fix**: Always TTS auto mode delivers voice notes as single messages with caption text on Telegram. Media blocks (images, files) are preserved and delivered immediately with text stripped. No text flash, no duplicate messages, no media loss.

- **What was not tested**: Other TTS providers (only Microsoft TTS tested live). Group chat TTS (tested in DM only). Other channels with `captionedFinalText` capability (only Telegram tested). Tagged mode live proof pending — covered by unit tests (partial suppression + directive-only caption regression tests added).

## Settle-lifecycle reconciliation (rebased onto current main)

Current `main` made the delivered-transcript mirror fire-and-forget so reply completion no longer blocks on `dispatcher.waitForIdle()`. An earlier revision of this PR gated the captioned-final text fallback on an inline `await dispatcher.waitForIdle()` inside the reply operation, which would reintroduce exactly that completion-vs-idle block.

The fallback now rides the same dispatcher settle lifecycle instead of an inline wait:

- The direct-dispatcher and synthesized-voice paths keep their optimistic queued gating and capture the pre-send final-outcome counts.
- When a captioned final (or its synthesized-voice sibling) is admitted through the raw dispatcher, a post-settlement task is registered via `registerReplyDispatcherSettledTask` — the same seam the transcript mirror uses. It runs after `waitForIdle()` inside `settleReplyDispatcher`, out of the reply hot path.
- That task compares the post-settlement final-outcome counts against the pre-send snapshot; if the captioned voice failed or cancelled asynchronously it re-sends the accumulated block text as a text-only final, so suppressed content is never silently dropped. On success it does nothing, so there is no duplicate text.

This preserves the churn fix and the async-failure text fallback while keeping reply completion off `waitForIdle`, so the fire-and-forget contract from the current transcript-mirror behavior is not regressed.

Closes #83511

target.title: feat(models): add provider request.timeoutMs and retry configuration
target.body:
## Summary

Adds two new model provider configuration fields:

1. **`models.providers.<id>.request.timeoutMs`** — Per-request timeout in milliseconds (max 600,000 / 10 min). Takes precedence over the existing provider-level `timeoutSeconds` when both are set. Useful for fast-failing serverless GPU cold starts where sub-second precision is needed.

2. **`models.providers.<id>.retry`** — Per-provider retry configuration for transient failures (timeouts, 5xx, connection resets). Fields:
   - `attempts` (1–5, default 1)
   - `minDelayMs` (default 500)
   - `maxDelayMs` (default 5,000)
   - `jitter` (default true)

   Schema and types are defined here; runtime retry-loop wiring will follow in a subsequent PR. Once wired, failed retries will exhaust before falling through to the next fallback model.

## Motivation

Serverless GPU providers (Modal, Replicate, etc.) can have variable cold-start times. The existing `timeoutSeconds` field works but only offers second-level granularity. `request.timeoutMs` gives operators millisecond-level control — critical when you want a provider to fail fast (e.g., 15s) and fall through to a backup model rather than waiting 120s+ on a cold start.

The `retry` config addresses the related question: "what happens when a transient failure occurs?" Currently OpenClaw falls through to the next model immediately. With `retry`, operators can opt into N retry attempts with exponential backoff before falling through.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/types.provider-request.ts` | Add `timeoutMs?: number` to `ConfiguredProviderRequest` |
| `src/config/types.models.ts` | Add `ModelProviderRetryConfig` type and `retry?` field on `ModelProviderConfig` |
| `src/config/zod-schema.core.ts` | Add `timeoutMs` to request fields, `ModelProviderRetrySchema`, `retry` on `ModelProviderSchema` |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model.ts` | `resolveProviderRequestTimeoutMsFromConfig()` checks `request.timeoutMs` first, then falls back to `timeoutSeconds` |
| `src/config/schema.help.ts` | Help text for `request.timeoutMs` and all `retry.*` fields |
| `src/config/schema.labels.ts` | UI labels for new fields |
| `src/config/zod-schema.provider-timeout-retry.test.ts` | 10 test cases: acceptance, bounds rejection, strict mode, backwards compat |

## Backwards Compatibility

- `timeoutSeconds` continues to work exactly as before
- `request.timeoutMs` is optional and only overrides when explicitly set
- `retry` is optional; without it, behavior is unchanged (immediate fallback)
- All new fields are `.optional()` in the Zod schema

## Testing

- [x] Schema validation tests: 10 cases covering acceptance, rejection (bounds, strict mode), and backwards compat
- [x] `tsc` import check passes
- [x] Generated JSON schema includes all new fields
- [ ] Full `vitest` suite (unable to run in sandbox due to memory constraints)

## Example Config

```yaml
models:
  providers:
    modal-agent:
      baseUrl: https://modal.com/v1
      timeoutSeconds: 120
      request:
        timeoutMs: 30000  # overrides timeoutSeconds at ms precision
      retry:
        attempts: 2
        minDelayMs: 500
        maxDelayMs: 5000
        jitter: true
      models:
        - id: zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8
          name: GLM-5.2
          reasoning: false
          input: [text]
          cost: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 }
          contextWindow: 131072
          maxTokens: 16384
```

target.body:
## Summary

- Restore Codex `before_prompt_build` hook input so plugins can observe loaded OpenClaw session messages again.
- Keep Codex app-server model input and `llm_input` diagnostics on the native thread path without mirrored OpenClaw history.
- Copy hook-observation messages per prompt-build pass so hook-side mutation cannot leak into a later prompt rebuild.

Fixes #88353

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Codex `before_prompt_build` no longer receives an empty `messages` array after session history has been loaded; Codex model input and `llm_input.historyMessages` still avoid mirrored OpenClaw history.
- **Real environment tested:** Local PR worktree after syncing `origin/main`, at HEAD `7758087aa855bf1c602484b34848048d625aa32c`, with installed dependencies and local `codex-cli 0.133.0` available as the Codex app-server command. The proof script imported the current worktree code and ran the real Codex app-server turn-construction path through the stdio app-server command.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```text
  source /media/vdc/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-89004-evidence/context.env
  cd "$TASK_WORKTREE"
  PROOF_HEAD="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" node --import tsx "$EVIDENCE_DIR/codex-app-server-hook-proof.mjs" 2>&1 | tee "$EVIDENCE_DIR/codex-app-server-hook-proof-after-sync.log"
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts --run --testNamePattern "applies before_prompt_build|keeps thread-start developer instructions stable|routes Codex model input diagnostics"
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.hooks.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.context-engine.test.ts --run --testNamePattern "before_prompt_build|llm_input|context engine|context-engine"
  OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/infra/boundary-file-read.test.ts src/infra/boundary-path.test.ts src/infra/hardlink-guards.test.ts src/infra/replace-file.test.ts src/infra/resolve-system-bin.test.ts src/infra/safe-package-install.test.ts src/infra/stable-node-path.test.ts src/infra/watch-node.test.ts --run
  pnpm exec oxfmt --threads=1 --check extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts
  git diff --check
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** The real app-server hook proof wrote `codex-app-server-hook-proof-output.json` and `codex-app-server-hook-proof-after-sync.log`. Terminal output excerpt:
  ```json
  {
    "hookEvents": [
      {
        "messagesLength": 1,
        "roles": ["assistant"],
        "text": "previous transcript marker CODEX-HOOK-PROOF-B2FAEC50"
      }
    ],
    "llmInputEvents": [
      {
        "promptIncludesHookContext": true,
        "historyMessagesLength": 0,
        "historyContainsPreviousTurn": false
      }
    ]
  }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts` now supplies a fresh copy of loaded `historyMessages` to `before_prompt_build`, so plugins observe the previous assistant turn. The Codex model-input and `llm_input` paths still read from the empty Codex-native history array. The new regression assertion also verifies a hook-side mutation from the first prompt-build pass is absent from the later prompt rebuild.
- **What was not tested:** The real app-server proof validated the hook/model-input boundary during turn construction, but the downstream Codex turn timed out waiting for completion in this environment after the proof point was captured. A full repository suite and a full successful live Codex assistant answer were not run.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix.

## CI failure attribution

- The visible failing current-head CI check was `checks-node-core-runtime-infra-file-safety` on PR head `efd74746717cefb83afa2b01c49f64cde1f92414`; its log showed Vitest produced no output for 900000ms and was terminated with exit code 143, not a failed assertion in this Codex patch.
- After syncing `origin/main`, the matching local infra file-safety target passed on HEAD `7758087aa855bf1c602484b34848048d625aa32c`: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 39 passed (39)`.

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001: The real proof still validates the changed hook/model-input boundary rather than a full downstream assistant answer. The downstream Codex turn timed out after the proof point was captured in this environment, so this remains disclosed under “What was not tested”; the changed behavior is covered by real app-server proof plus focused and adjacent regression tests.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the touched contract because the production change remains narrowly scoped to the Codex app-server hook/model-input boundary, and the new assertion covers the reviewer-suggested mutation isolation case.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** History-sensitive plugins using `before_prompt_build.messages` can again distinguish a resumed Codex session from a brand-new session, without re-injecting mirrored OpenClaw transcript history into the native Codex model input.
- **What did NOT change:** This does not change Codex `turn/start` model input history, `llm_input.historyMessages`, provider routing, plugin APIs, generated protocol/schema files, dependencies, workflows, lockfiles, or any non-Codex extension behavior.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth stays split by owner: loaded OpenClaw `historyMessages` are only the hook-observation input, while Codex native thread continuity remains owned by the app-server thread and current `turn/start.input`; the proof and tests verify that the model-consumed history path stays empty.
- **Patch quality notes:** The patch avoids fallback behavior and keeps the two channels explicit: hook observation gets copied loaded session messages, while Codex model input and diagnostics keep the empty native-thread history. No dependencies, generated files, workflows, lockfiles, or cross-extension public APIs were changed.
- **Target test file:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** A session with a previous assistant message calls `before_prompt_build`; the hook sees that previous message, while the Codex turn input still contains only the current prompt/context and diagnostics keep history empty.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The focused regression locks the broken public hook surface and the adjacent mutation-isolation case without asserting unrelated Codex runtime implementation details or broad session replay behavior.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** availability, session-state, plugin-contract.
- **Risk explanation:** The touched surface is in the Codex app-server prompt-build path, so a mistake could affect Codex turn construction or plugin prompt shaping for resumed sessions.
- **Why acceptable:** The production diff only changes the input passed to `before_prompt_build`; the Codex model-input history array remains empty, `llm_input.historyMessages` remains empty in proof, focused/adjacent tests passed, and the matching local infra file-safety shard passed after syncing main.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The Codex app-server path reused the empty `codexModelInputHistoryMessages` array for `before_prompt_build`. That array exists to keep mirrored OpenClaw transcript history out of Codex native model input, but the hook contract is separate and should observe the already-loaded OpenClaw session messages.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The patch fixes the source contract invariant instead of masking the symptom: hook observation and Codex model input are separate channels, so `before_prompt_build` receives loaded session messages while Codex model input and `llm_input` diagnostics continue to use the empty Codex-native history array. The hook input is now copied per prompt-build pass so plugin mutation cannot alter later prompt construction.

target.title: fix(gateway): support native Windows exec approvals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The released Windows companion returns a host-native exec-approval policy from `system.execApprovals.get` and accepts that policy on `system.execApprovals.set`. OpenClaw's dedicated `exec.approvals.node.*` path assumed every node used the OpenClaw approvals-file shape, so Windows policy reads, writes, and Control UI rendering were incorrect.

Closes the surviving approvals slice of #88163.

## Why This Change Was Made

- add a node-specific protocol snapshot that accepts either the existing file-backed shape or the shipped Windows-native shape without weakening the existing gateway snapshot contract
- validate node snapshots at the Gateway boundary before CLI or Control UI consumes them
- relay native writes without translating them into an approvals file, require the current hash, and require an explicit full rule list because the Windows setter replaces all rules
- expose native policy get/set in the CLI; keep Control UI native policies read-only
- preserve generated Swift protocol models and document the two policy shapes

The remaining #88163 changes are intentionally excluded: loopback auth, command exposure, raw invoke blocking, build tooling, and pairing behavior have either landed independently or changed architecture on current `main`.

## User Impact

Windows companion nodes can be inspected with `openclaw approvals get --node ...` and updated with `openclaw approvals set --node ...`. Concurrent writes are hash-guarded. Control UI displays the native policy without offering the incompatible approvals-file editor. Existing file-backed gateway, macOS, and headless-node behavior remains unchanged.

## Evidence

- released Windows contract inspected at `openclaw-windows-node` `v0.6.12`: [get and constraints](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v0.6.12/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/SystemCapability.cs#L643-L681), [hash-guarded replacement set](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v0.6.12/src/OpenClaw.Shared/Capabilities/SystemCapability.cs#L684-L782), and [canonical rules/actions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/v0.6.12/src/OpenClaw.Shared/ExecApprovalPolicy.cs#L15-L41)
- Blacksmith Testbox [run 28866599783](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28866599783): focused protocol, Gateway, CLI, and UI suite; 45 tests passed across four Vitest shards
- Blacksmith Testbox: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:test:packages`, and `tsgo:test:ui` passed
- protocol and Swift generators rerun; generated Swift output byte-stable
- `oxfmt --check` on all touched TypeScript/Markdown and `git diff --check` passed
- exact-current autoreview completed before commit

Proof gap: no active Windows Crabbox/pond lease was available for a fresh native Windows run. This change is therefore proved against the released companion source contract plus exact Gateway/CLI/UI integration tests, not a new physical Windows session.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI session reseed history renders all user messages with the hardcoded `User:` label, making group chat participants indistinguishable in the prompt the model sees. In group chats (Matrix, Discord, Telegram), the model cannot tell which participant said what — sender metadata (`senderLabel`, `senderName`, `senderUsername`, `senderId`) is already present on transcript message objects but was never read by `renderHistoryMessage()`.

Related to #98229.

## Why This Change Was Made

The renderer is the right layer — sender metadata is already populated on message objects by channel inbound pipelines (Discord, Matrix, Telegram). This PR reads those fields at render time without touching persistence, avoiding architectural conflict with #90552 (durable sender metadata persistence).

What changed:
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts`: `HistoryMessage` type (+4 sender fields), `coerceSenderLabel()` sanitizer, `resolveSenderField()` envelope reader, sender-aware user role rendering in `renderHistoryMessage()`
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts`: +14 test cases

Design decisions:
- Sender label nested as `User (Alice): text`, never replacing the `User` role — prevents role spoofing
- Fallback chain: `senderLabel → senderName → senderUsername → senderId → "User"`
- Top-level fields take priority over `__openclaw` envelope (in-memory pipeline > persisted metadata)
- CR/LF stripped from sender labels — prevents transcript line injection
- Assistant/compactionSummary rendering unchanged

Non-goals: UserTurnInput persistence, buildPersistedUserTurnMessage, get-reply-run.ts, gateway chat paths — all deferred to #90552.

## User Impact

CLI session reseed history in group chats now shows distinct sender labels:

```
User (Alice): What's the weather?
Assistant: 22°C and sunny.
User (Bob): Add a meeting at 2pm
Assistant: Done! Meeting at 2pm.
```

Direct/1:1 sessions without sender metadata see no change (`User: hello`). Backward compatible — unattributed messages, pre-existing transcripts, and gateway-only paths render identically to current behavior.

## Evidence

Commit `58680ff374`. Proof script: `scripts/proof-sender-label.mjs`.

### Tests — 36 passed

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

### Live output: `node --import tsx scripts/proof-sender-label.mjs`

**Scenario 1: Multi-sender group chat (Matrix/Discord-style)**
```
User (Alice (PM)): Hey team, what's the status on the API migration?
Assistant: Running ahead of schedule — ETA tomorrow EOD.
User (Bob (Engineer)): I found a bug in the auth middleware, filing an issue now.
Assistant: Thanks Bob, can you share the issue number?
User (Carol (Designer)): The design specs are ready in Figma, link in thread.
Assistant: Great, I'll review and get back with feedback.
User (Dave (Intern)): Can someone help me with the deployment pipeline?
```
✅ Distinct labels. User role preserved. Assistant messages not decorated.

**Scenario 2: Fallback chain**
```
User (Alice): has senderLabel
User (Bob): has senderName only
User (carol_42): has senderUsername only
User (U123456): has senderId only
User: no sender fields at all
```

**Scenario 3: `__openclaw` envelope fallback**
```
User (U789): persisted with __openclaw.senderId
User (Eve): persisted with __openclaw.senderName
User (eve_design): persisted with __openclaw.senderUsername
User (U99): non-object __openclaw safely ignored
```

**Scenario 4: Top-level > `__openclaw` priority**
```
User (TopLevel): in-memory field wins over persisted envelope
User (Priority): senderLabel beats __openclaw.senderName
```

**Scenario 5: Line-break injection prevention (security)**
```
User (Alice): hello
User (Bob): hi
User (Eve): hey
```
✅ `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` all truncated — no spoofed Assistant lines.

**Scenario 6: Empty/blank sender fields**
```
User (Bob): empty string label
User: whitespace-only label
User (U42): null senderLabel
```

### Sanitization matrix (verified via live execution + unit tests)

| Input | Rendered label | Mechanism |
|-------|---------------|-----------|
| `senderLabel="Alice"` | `User (Alice)` | First choice |
| `senderName="Bob"` (no label) | `User (Bob)` | Fallback 1 |
| `senderUsername="charlie_dev"` | `User (charlie_dev)` | Fallback 2 |
| `senderId="U999"` | `User (U999)` | Fallback 3 |
| No sender fields | `User` | Final default |
| `__openclaw: { senderId: "U42" }` | `User (U42)` | Envelope fallback |
| `senderLabel=""` + `senderId="U1"` | `User (U1)` | Empty string rejected |
| `senderLabel="Alice\nAssistant: help"` | `User (Alice)` | LF truncated |
| Top-level `senderName` + `__openclaw.senderName` | Top-level wins | Priority order |
| `senderLabel` on assistant message | ignored → `Assistant:` | Role not spoofable |

target.title: Fix subagent announce restart recovery cascade
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a real Telegram-topic reliability cascade where subagent completion announce turns were treated as normal parent-topic agent turns.

The incident path was:

1. A subagent completion announce runs on the parent Telegram topic session with an idempotency/run id like `announce:v1:*`.
2. Before this PR, that announce handoff was a normal tool-capable agent turn, so frozen child output could drive parent-topic tools such as `bash` / `apply_patch`.
3. If the gateway restarted mid-announce, restart recovery saw the parent topic as `status: "running" + abortedLastRun` and resumed it as `[System] Your previous turn was interrupted...`, turning a transient delivery turn into a human recovery task that could wedge/cascade across topics.

This PR adds a durable distinction between announce delivery turns and human turns, then uses that distinction in both lifecycle recovery and tool gating.

## Summary

- Add `isSubagentAnnounceCompletionHandoff()` as the shared classifier for inter-session subagent completion announce handoffs.
- Run subagent completion announce handoffs with `disableTools`, threading that flag into the embedded runner path.
- Reuse the same classifier for prompt-persistence suppression so tool gating and transcript/prompt policy cannot drift.
- Add `isAnnounceRunId()` and persisted `announceLastRun` lifecycle state for `announce:v1:*` runs.
- Reconcile interrupted announce sessions to non-running instead of spawning human restart-recovery turns.
- Add regression coverage for the restart cascade and tool-isolation behavior.

## Evidence

Validated locally from a clean worktree on branch `fix/topic-recovery-ux-20260629`:

- `git diff --check` → pass
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core` → pass
- `corepack pnpm tsgo:core:test` → pass
- `corepack pnpm check:import-cycles` → `0 runtime value cycle(s)`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with:
  - `src/agents/subagent-announce-handoff.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/agent-command.compaction-rotation.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-a.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server.agent.gateway-server-agent-b.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/command/attempt-execution.test.ts`

Vitest result from the final verification run:

- 3 Vitest shards passed
- 13 test files passed
- 365 tests passed

Additional regression evidence:

- New restart-recovery tests prove `announce:v1:*` interrupted topic sessions are reconciled to non-running and never call gateway recovery.
- New agent-command test proves subagent completion announce handoffs set `disableTools: true`.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix: reclaim superseded reply turns
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users in Telegram-visible conversations could see a reply run get acknowledged or superseded, then have a previously aborted reply turn remain in the active in-memory lane and block the next visible reply for that topic.

In dogfood use this showed up as a Telegram topic appearing stuck even though the older reply run had already been aborted and no useful final answer was going to arrive from it.

## Why This Change Was Made

This updates reply-turn admission so an aborted superseded run can be reclaimed when the matching persisted run record is terminal. The reclaim stays bounded to the same session key and superseded run id, so a genuinely active reply run is still protected from accidental double admission.

The regression coverage exercises the stale aborted/superseded lane and keeps the existing active-run protection intact.

AI-assisted: yes. This was investigated and implemented through an AI-assisted local OpenClaw repair workflow, then manually re-verified with focused tests and formatting checks.

## User Impact

Telegram and other auto-reply surfaces should no longer need a manual session/topic reset for this specific stale superseded-reply lane class. A newer message can reclaim the stale aborted turn once OpenClaw can prove the old run is terminal.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` at head `87434a7b80b82cdc3495120b54a7a8b9bedca9d7`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101552: `Promise.all` over all agent usage queries created an unbounded array of concurrent database operations. For deployments with 100+ agents, this instantly saturated the SQLite WAL lock and connection pool, causing `SQLITE_BUSY` timeouts or memory spikes when the usage dashboard loaded.

Replaced `Promise.all` with `runTasksWithConcurrency({ limit: 8 })` to cap simultaneous usage queries against the shared state database. This prevents SQLite starvation while keeping dashboard load times reasonable.

## User Impact

- Large multi-agent deployments no longer crash or timeout when opening the usage dashboard
- Dashboard load time slightly increases for very large agent counts (expected and acceptable)

target.title: fix(infra): attach error listener to detached spawn in update handoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`startManagedServiceUpdateHandoff()` in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff.ts` spawns a detached child process with `child.unref()` but no `'error'` listener. When spawn fails (e.g. execPath invalid, permissions changed), Node.js emits an async `'error'` event on the ChildProcess. Without a listener, this crashes the parent as an unhandled error.

This is the same pattern identified and fixed in #101392 for `process-respawn.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The spawn at line 731 creates a detached handoff process during managed service updates. If the executable path is invalid, the async `'error'` event crashes the parent gateway.

## Evidence

### Before: no error listener → unhandled crash

```
$ node -e "const{spawn}=require('child_process');spawn('/nonexistent',[],{detached:true,stdio:'ignore'})"
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^
Error: spawn /nonexistent ENOENT
```

### After: error listener attached → graceful handling

```
$ node -e "
const {spawn} = require('child_process');
const child = spawn('/nonexistent', [], {detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'});
child.on('error', () => {});
console.log('OK: process does not crash');
"
OK: process does not crash
```

### Test mock updated

Updated `spawnMock` in `update-managed-service-handoff.test.ts` to include `on: vi.fn()` in the return value — required because the production code now calls `child.on("error", ...)`.

## Merge Risk

Low. The change adds a no-op error listener before `child.unref()`. Test mock updated accordingly.

target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads the previous session transcript with an unbounded `fs.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the reset-hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset-hook transcript reader is now routed through the existing streaming session transcript reader (`readSessionMessagesAsync`), which already caps reads and supports archive fallback. This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving previous-session messages for `before_reset` hooks.

`storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope and by both runtime callers:
- the normal `/new`/`/reset` command handlers in `commands-reset.ts`, and
- the missed-reset-hook fallback in `get-reply.ts`.

This keeps custom-store transcript resolution consistent across both entry points.

## User Impact

Reset hooks now receive previous session messages safely even for very large transcripts, without risking process OOM, and custom store paths continue to resolve correctly on both command and fallback paths.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests that mock `readSessionMessagesAsync` and verify the reader scope (`sessionId`, `sessionFile`, `sessionKey`, `storePath`, `agentId`) and the `allowResetArchiveFallback` option.
- Added focused coverage proving `storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope for custom-store sessions.
- Added fallback-caller coverage in `get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts` proving `storePath` reaches `emitResetCommandHooks` when inline actions return early.
- Local focused runs pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run` (6/6 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run` (12/12 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts --run` (3/3 tests)

target.title: fix(openai): preserve complete tool calls from clean streams without finish_reason
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible providers that emit `delta.tool_calls` during streaming but terminate with `data: [DONE]` without a final `finish_reason` chunk (e.g. Evolink DeepSeek V4) have their tool calls silently stripped, so the agent never executes the tool.
- Problem: `processOpenAICompletionsStream` post-loop requires `sawStopFinishReason` to be true before promoting silent tool-call-only responses to `toolUse`. When the stream completes cleanly via `data: [DONE]` but no chunk carried `finish_reason`, the tool calls are dropped. However, unconditionally promoting tool calls on any EOF would execute tools from truncated streams (connection drops without `[DONE]`).
- Solution: Track two signals independently. `sawNativeToolCallDelta` is set when structured `delta.tool_calls` arrives. `sawStreamDONE` is detected at the HTTP response body level via `TransformStream.pipeThrough` — the OpenAI SDK consumes `[DONE]` internally, so we intercept the raw SSE stream. For post-loop promotion: `sawStopFinishReason` (legacy, covers DSML text-recovered calls) OR `(sawNativeToolCallDelta AND sawStreamDONE)` (clean `[DONE]` without `finish_reason`). EOF without `[DONE]` remains fail-closed.
- What changed: `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts` (add `sawNativeToolCallDelta` + `sawStreamDONE`; intercept fetch with `TransformStream` to detect `data: [DONE]` in raw SSE body; update promotion to `(sawStopFinishReason || (sawNativeToolCallDelta && sawStreamDONE))`), `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts` (update test + add 2 new tests including no-`[DONE]` fail-closed case)
- What did NOT change: DSML-recovered tool call behavior (still requires `sawStopFinishReason`), the `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` strip guard, `finalizeTransportStream` / `failTransportStream` paths

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #97994
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Providers like Evolink's `deepseek-v4-pro` stream valid `delta.tool_calls` with `data: [DONE]` as the stream terminator but no `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` chunk. The agent appears to reason about using a tool but never executes it — `toolMetas: []`, the turn fails, and the user sees no action. Non-streaming requests to the same provider return `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` correctly.

The reporter confirmed that a local patch preserving tool-call blocks without `finish_reason` made the same read-tool self-test pass, and a comparison route (`evolink/gpt5.5`) in the same OpenClaw setup did not show the issue.

The non-transport `openai-completions.ts` path already promotes on `(stopReason === "stop" && hasToolCalls && !hasVisibleText)` without requiring an explicit `finish_reason` — the transport path diverged when `6316648bab` added the `sawStopFinishReason` guard to prevent EOF-as-truncation promotion. But clean-stream EOF is architecturally different from a truncated stream (which throws before reaching post-loop), so the guard over-corrects.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Streaming tool-call-only responses without `finish_reason` were dropped; they are now promoted to `toolUse`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node.js v22.19.0, branch `fix/openai-stream-no-finish-tool-97994`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Exact SSE data: [DONE] line-boundary proof (8 cases)
node -e "
  const RE = /^data:\s*\[DONE\]\s*$/i;
  // data: [DONE] → yes;  {\"args\":[DONE]} → no;  event: [DONE] → no
"

# 2. Loopback SSE proof through createOpenAICompletionsTransportStreamFn
#    (real HTTP server → fetch wrapper → TransformStream → promotion gating)
node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # [DONE] without finish_reason
node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # EOF without [DONE]

# 3. Vitest regression suite (18 tests across 2 projects)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts \
  -t 'cleanly without finish_reason|visible text and no finish_reason|does not promote native|does not authorize recovered DeepSeek|finish_reason stop|finish_reason tool_calls'
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node -e "..."   # Exact SSE data: [DONE] parsing

exact data: [DONE]                            ✅ detected
data:[DONE] (no space)                        ✅ detected
data: [DONE] (trailing)                       ✅ detected
content with [DONE] inside                    ✅ rejected
tool_calls containing [DONE]                  ✅ rejected
comment line with [DONE]                      ✅ rejected
event: [DONE] (wrong field)                   ✅ rejected
```

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-loopback.mjs   # real HTTP → fetch wrapper → promotion

=== Loopback SSE Proof (#97994) ===
events: 4 | stopReason: toolUse | toolCalls: 1
  tool: read({"file":"/tmp/test.txt"})

✅ PASS — loopback SSE: [DONE] without finish_reason → toolUse
```

```console
$ node --import tsx proof-loopback-eof.mjs   # EOF without [DONE]

=== Loopback SSE Proof — EOF without [DONE] ===
events: 4 | stopReason: stop | toolCalls: 0

✅ PASS — EOF without [DONE] remains fail-closed
```

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --run src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts -t '...'
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  18 passed | 558 skipped (568)
```| Input scenario | sawStreamDONE | stopReason | tool calls retained | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, no text | N/A | `toolUse` | ✅ yes | executes tools |
| `finish_reason: "stop"`, no text | N/A | `toolUse` | ✅ yes | executes tools (#88791) |
| **native tool calls + `finish_reason: null` + `[DONE]`** | ✅ true | **`toolUse`** | ✅ **yes** | **executes tools (this fix)** |
| **native tool calls + `finish_reason: null` + EOF only** | ❌ false | **`stop`** | **❌ no (stripped)** | **fail-closed (safety)** |
| tool calls + visible text, `finish_reason: null` | N/A | `stop` | ❌ no | conservative (ambiguous) |
| DSML-recovered + no `finish_reason` + `[DONE]` | N/A | `stop` | ❌ no | DSML still requires `finish_reason` |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. Native `delta.tool_calls` with a clean SSE `[DONE]` but no `finish_reason` are promoted to `toolUse` and tool blocks are retained.
  2. Native `delta.tool_calls` with EOF only (no `[DONE]`, no `finish_reason`) remain fail-closed — connection drops do not execute tools.
  3. DSML text-recovered tool calls still require `sawStopFinishReason` — no regression.
  4. All existing behaviors are unchanged.
- **What was not tested**: Live Evolink API endpoint (no API key); non-streaming fallback via that exact provider.

### Live Provider Regression Proof (DeepSeek Official API)

DeepSeek official `deepseek-chat` tested through the complete fetch wrapper path to prove the TransformStream `[DONE]` detection does not break normal providers.

```console
=== DeepSeek Live Regression Proof (#98124) ===
API key: sk-ef782...b866
Model: deepseek-chat
Base URL: https://api.deepseek.com/v1

[model-fetch] start provider=deepseek api=openai-completions model=deepseek-chat ...
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=372 contentType=text/event-stream
Events: 12 | types: start, text_start, text_delta, done
Done reason: stop
✅ text response completed normally
✅ stream completed without errors
✅ fetch wrapper + TransformStream handled real SSE without issues

✅ PASS — DeepSeek official API regression proof: fix does not break normal providers
```

- **Verified**: Real SSE stream → fetch wrapper → TransformStream → OpenAI SDK consumption. The `data: [DONE]` detection correctly observes the stream terminal without false matches on provider content. Normal provider behavior is unchanged.
- **Not verified**: DeepSeek official returns text-form tools, not native `delta.tool_calls`, so the promotion path was not exercised via this provider. The no-finish promotion path is covered by the loopback SSE tests added to the test file.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`processOpenAICompletionsStream` in `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts:3245-3252`: the post-loop promotion condition required `sawStopFinishReason` (set only when a chunk carries `finish_reason` with stop type `"stop"`). When the stream completes cleanly (for-await exits normally) but no chunk carries `finish_reason`, the promotion is skipped and the downstream `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` guard strips the parsed tool-call blocks.

**Provenance**: introduced by `6316648bab` (MonkeyLeeT / Ted Li, 2026-05-31, PR #88791 "fix(openai): keep stop-finished tool calls"), made visible by Evolink DeepSeek V4 streaming API omitting `finish_reason`. Confidence: **clear**.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file**: `src/agents/openai-transport-stream.test.ts`
- **Covered scenarios**: clean-stream no-finish promotion, visible-text no-finish conservative strip, `finish_reason: "stop"` promotion (regression), `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` promotion (regression), `finish_reason: "stop"` with visible text strip (regression)
- **Minimal guard rationale**: The `hasToolCalls && stopReason !== "toolUse"` post-loop strip guard and the `!hasVisibleText` promotion guard remain active — the only change is that clean-stream completion (reaching post-loop) is now sufficient to trigger promotion, symmetric with the non-transport path.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Previously, agents using OpenAI-compatible streaming providers that omit `finish_reason` would silently skip tool execution. After this fix, those tool calls execute normally. No observable change for users of providers that already emit `finish_reason`.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No (tool calls were already parsed and structured; this fix only promotes them to execution when the stream completes cleanly — same safety contract as the `finish_reason: "stop"` path)
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios**: Clean-stream no-finish tool calls promoted (tsx runtime), visible-text no-finish tool calls stripped (vitest), all regression tests pass
- **Edge cases checked**: Mixed text+tool-calls without finish_reason (conservative strip), clean-stream with finish_reason (unchanged), finish_reason="tool_calls" (unchanged)
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live Evolink endpoint behavior, truncated stream error-path behavior (throws before post-loop, architecturally unchanged)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — existing behaviors for `finish_reason`-bearing providers are unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — adding `sawNativeToolCallDelta` + `sawStreamDONE` gives the post-loop a structured-provider signal gated by a clean SSE terminal. The `TransformStream.pipeThrough` interceptor detects `data: [DONE]` before the OpenAI SDK consumes it, distinguishing clean termination from connection drops. This matches ClawSweeper's recommendation: "[P1] Carry an explicit clean SSE terminal signal so [DONE] without finish_reason promotes tool calls while EOF without [DONE] remains fail-closed."
- **Safety guard**: EOF without `[DONE]` (connection drop, truncated response) remains fail-closed because `sawStreamDONE` is never set. The `(sawNativeToolCallDelta && sawStreamDONE)` conjunction ensures both conditions: provider signaled tool-use intent AND stream terminated cleanly.
- **Alternative considered**:
  - Adding a separate `!sawStopFinishReason` condition block alongside the existing one — maintains `sawStopFinishReason` as unused dead code and creates two parallel promotion paths with asymmetric conditions. Rejected: less clean, harder to audit.
  - Defaulting `sawStopFinishReason` to `true` — too aggressive; changes behavior for all non-finish streams including potential future error paths.
  - Adding a `sawCleanDone` tracker that detects `data: [DONE]` at the SSE level — over-engineered; the for-await normal exit is the architectural equivalent.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: See commit message and PR body for full analysis chain (provenance → root cause → invariant → fix → test matrix).

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: A provider that streams tool calls but the connection drops mid-stream without throwing (extremely rare — Node fetch typically throws on TCP reset). Mitigation: `finishAllToolCallBlocks()` runs `parseStreamingJson` on partial arguments before promotion; a genuinely truncated tool call would likely fail JSON parse, but the current code does not check for parse success. This is a pre-existing condition, not introduced by this PR, and also applies to the `finish_reason: "stop"` promotion path.
- **Compatibility**: No breaking change. Providers that emit `finish_reason` are unaffected. Providers that omit it now get correct tool execution.
- **Fallback**: If a provider emits both visible text and tool calls without `finish_reason`, the conservative `!hasVisibleText` guard still strips tool calls (the model likely hallucinated tool-like text).

---

Fixes #97994

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```
